## Operator attestation — Titan embedding reachable from the Gerrit instance role

The `[non-codebase]` acceptance criterion is now satisfied by a live
before/after call, not by simulation and not from an operator identity
holding `bedrock:*`, per the evidentiary standard in `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:20-55`.

**Change under attestation**

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| Gerrit change | 3212 (MERGED) |
| Change-Id | `I434df308687c03cbe456693954ba3363ed1e9cec` |
| Revision SHA | `213341e3e58faf021f51ddd7db0285f57d95f2b9` |
| Applied from | `origin/main` = `af769ead9febdb49484b78c0bbb1bc4fb2480e34` |
| Operator identity (apply) | `arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier` |
| Calling identity (probe) | `arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5` |

**Terraform**

`scripts/terraform_prod.py plan` reported `Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to
destroy` — exactly this ticket's edit (Titan ARN added to the resource list,
sid renamed to `InvokeScopedBedrockModels`), with both Claude ARNs and the
action list untouched. No drift was present in the deployed tree. The apply
reported `Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed`.

**Before/after control**

The call is the same in both runs: `bedrock-runtime invoke-model` against
`arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`,
issued over SSM `AWS-RunShellScript` on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` so it runs
under the scoped instance role.

- **Before apply, 2026-11-02T17:44:19Z — DENIED.**
  `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel
  on resource: arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
  because no identity-based policy allows the bedrock:InvokeModel action`
- **After apply, 2026-11-02T17:45:09Z — OK.**
  Embedding returned, **dimensions 1024**, input tokens 9.

The denial immediately before the apply is what makes this evidence rather
than a bare success: it rules out the grant having already been present by
some other path.

**Regression check on the shared statement**

This ticket widened a policy statement the review-bot also depends on, so
Claude was re-checked from the same instance role after the apply:
`bedrock-runtime converse` against `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` returned
normally. The existing grant is intact.

**Not verified here:** that the running review-bot container picks the
credential up without a restart. The role's permissions are what this ticket
changed, and those are confirmed.
